summary: Allocates and initializes a keyframe array on `this` from input 3D position data. Guards on a2 being non-null and a3 >= 4, runs a utility initializer, stores the keyframe count at this+0x4, allocates 28*a3+4 heap bytes (4-byte count header plus a3 elements of 28 bytes each), stores the element pointer at this+0x0, copies a3 DWORD-position triples into the elements, then pre-computes the accumulated keyframe arc lengths via sub_457EE0. Returns 0 on success, 1 on invalid input.

operations.description: Guard on (a2 != 0 && a3 >= 4); when false the function returns the result 1 immediately.
Call the utility initializer UtilityFunction_8020 with no arguments before allocation.
Store the requested keyframe count a3 at this+0x4.
Allocate heap memory of size 28*a3 + 4 via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper; the returned block holds a 4-byte count header followed by a3 keyframe elements of 28 bytes each.
Write the count a3 into the header (first DWORD of the allocation) and store the element pointer (header + 4 bytes) at this+0x0; on allocation failure the stored element pointer is null.
Guard on the stored keyframe count at this+0x4 being greater than 0 before entering the copy loop.

Loop over all a3 keyframes, copying each input DWORD position triple (v9[0..2]) into a 28-byte element of the array at this+0x0, advancing the source by three DWORDs and the destination by 28 bytes per iteration.
Pre-compute the cumulative arc length for each keyframe in the newly allocated array by calling sub_457EE0 on the keyframe object.
Return 0 on successful allocation and initialization, or 1 when the input guard (a2 null or a3 < 4) fails.

unresolved: The exact meaning of the three-DWORD position triple (world space vs. path-local coordinates) is caller-defined.
The identity and behavior of UtilityFunction_8020 and the layout consumed by sub_457EE0 are not established here.
